patients.summary: Software developer in Amherst who carries a sickle cell trait label alongside a sickle cell disease course on hydroxyurea and folic acid. Folate deficiency found at a 2023 fatigue visit; hyposthenuria and CKD stage 2 named by nephrology in 2024; preconception counseling with his wife in 2026.

documents.author: front desk
documents.body: Caller is a 23 y/o man moving his primary care to us after relocating to Amherst for work. Reports sickle cell, on two daily meds that his old office has been refilling. Membership paperwork emailed. Records release signed electronically for his prior primary care office. New patient visit booked 9/8 at 9:00.

documents.title: Records from prior primary care office
documents.author: front desk
documents.body:
Records from prior primary care office, covering 2016 through June 2021. Received by fax, 34 pages, routed to PCP before the new patient visit.

Problem list on their summary: sickle cell trait (newborn screen); recurrent vaso-occlusive pain crises; sickle cell disease without crisis.
Medications on their summary: hydroxyurea 500 mg capsules, 2 caps daily; folic acid 1 mg daily.
Allergies: NKDA.
Immunizations listed as current, last Tdap 2016.
Visits: yearly physicals, pain episodes handled at home by phone, CBCs every few months. No admissions in the period covered. Most recent CBC (06/2021) hemoglobin in the mid 9s, MCV just over 100.

documents.title: New Patient Visit
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
NEW PATIENT VISIT

23 y/o man here to set up care. Moved to the area this summer for a developer job. Prior PCP records reviewed (filed 9/1).

Sickle cell: labelled trait on his newborn screen and every list since, but describes a lifelong disease course. Painful episodes in arms, legs and low back since early childhood; several admissions as a child and teen for IV pain medicine. Nothing needing the hospital in the last several years. Now gets milder flares every few weeks; rests, pushes oral fluids, rides them out at home. Has been on hydroxyurea for years (1000 mg daily) and folic acid 1 mg daily, refilled through his old office.

PMH: as above. PSH: none.
Meds: hydroxyurea 500 mg x2 daily; folic acid 1 mg daily.
Allergies: NKDA.
Family: father has sickle cell trait; a cousin on mother's side has sickle cell disease; mother with hypertension.
Social: software developer, works mostly remote. Never smoker. No alcohol. Married.
Immunizations: reports current; Tdap 2016 per old records.

ROS: energy his usual. No fever, chest pain, dyspnea, urinary symptoms, rash.

Exam: Well appearing, slim. Mild conjunctival pallor, no scleral icterus. No lymphadenopathy. Heart regular, soft systolic flow murmur at the left sternal border. Lungs clear. Abdomen soft, nontender, spleen not felt. No leg ulcers. Neuro grossly normal.

A/P
1. Sickle cell (trait per records, disease course, on hydroxyurea): continue hydroxyurea 1000 mg daily and folic acid. Baseline CBC with retic, LDH, CMP, UA today. CBC every 3-4 months while on hydroxyurea; will take over the refills.
2. Recurrent pain crises: stable pattern, home management. Hydration, call us for anything that does not settle.
3. Health maintenance: HIV and hep C screen today. Flu shot when available next month. PHQ-2 negative.

Follow up in about 6 months, sooner with any problems.

documents.title: Your lab results
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: Hi Andre, your labs from Wednesday are back. Hemoglobin 9.6 with a reticulocyte count of 6.2% and LDH 334: right in line with the numbers in your old records. Kidney and liver tests fine apart from the mildly raised bilirubin we expect with sickle cell. Urine normal. HIV and hepatitis C screens negative. No changes. Next blood count in December.

documents.title: Annual Physical
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
ANNUAL PHYSICAL

Feels well. Pain flares continue at the same rhythm, every few weeks, short, home-managed. Nothing near needing the ED. Working long hours but sleeping ok. Walks most evenings.

Meds: hydroxyurea 1000 mg daily, folic acid 1 mg daily. NKDA.
Social: never smoker, no alcohol.

Exam: Pleasant, well. Conjunctivae a little pale, sclerae anicteric. Oropharynx normal. No nodes. Soft systolic flow murmur LSB, otherwise RRR. Lungs clear. Abdomen soft, no splenomegaly. Skin: no ulcers. Neuro nonfocal.

PHQ-2: 0.

Plan:
- Sickle cell on hydroxyurea: CBC/retic/LDH, CMP today. Continue both meds.
- Lipids once for baseline.
- Flu and bivalent COVID booster given.
- Continue CBCs every 3-4 months. Physical again next September.

conditions.label: Folate deficiency due to increased requirement from erythroid hyperplasia

procedures.procedure: Office visit, established patient, moderate MDM

documents.title: Office Visit - Fatigue
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
CC: tired and weak for several months.

HPI: 25 y/o with sickle cell (trait per his records, disease course, on hydroxyurea). Over the past few months he has less stamina: the stairs up to his apartment wear him out, and now and then he gets lightheaded if he gets up fast. No bleeding of any kind, no black stools, no fever, nothing viral recently. Eating ok, not great; regular mixed diet. Pain flares unchanged, mild, every few weeks, none needing a hospital in the past year.

Meds: hydroxyurea 1000 mg daily (takes reliably). Folic acid 1 mg daily: on questioning, misses it a lot, maybe half the days.
NKDA.

Exam: Vitals in normal range today, no orthostatic drop. Conjunctivae pale. No jaundice. No lymph nodes. Soft systolic flow murmur, regular rhythm. Lungs clear. Abdomen soft and benign, no spleen tip. Neuro normal.

Assessment/plan:
- Fatigue with worse anemia than his baseline. CBC with diff, retic, LDH, liver panel, folate and B12 sent today.
- Suspect folate is running short given how often he skips it and the turnover from hemolysis. Reviewed why the folic acid matters more for him than for most people. He will set a daily phone alarm and use a weekly pill box.
- Continue hydroxyurea.
- Recheck CBC in about 8 weeks. Return precautions for chest pain, shortness of breath, fainting, or a pain flare that won't settle.

documents.title: Anemia workup results
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
Hgb 8.8 (his usual is mid 9s), MCV 112, retic 8%, WBC 7.2, plt 430, T bili 2.3, LDH 418. Folate 2.4, low. B12 486, normal.

Impression: folate deficiency from the increased demand of his erythroid hyperplasia, on top of missed doses. Same 1 mg dose with daily adherence; added to problem list. Recheck early May.

documents.title: Your blood work
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: Andre, your folate level came back low at 2.4, and your hemoglobin is 8.8, a bit below where you usually sit. Sickle cell marrow works overtime and burns through folate, so the folic acid really has to be every single day. B12 is normal. Keep the hydroxyurea the same. Let's recheck in about 8 weeks; the front desk will reach out. If you feel worse before then, message me or call.

documents.title: RE: Your blood work
documents.author: patient
documents.body: Got it, thanks. Alarm is set. Feels kind of dumb that it was the cheapest pill.

documents.title: Office Visit - Urinary Frequency
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
S: About 2 months of urinating much more often, day and night, up 2-3 times most nights. Drinks a lot of water, always has, partly for the sickle cell. No dysuria, no blood in urine, no fever or flank/back pain beyond his usual flares. Not thirsty out of proportion. More tired, he thinks from broken sleep.
Meds unchanged: hydroxyurea, folic acid. NKDA.

O: Vitals normal. Well appearing. No CVA tenderness. Abdomen soft. Mild pallor, murmur as before.
UA (dip in office): SG 1.006; protein, glucose, blood negative.

A/P: Polyuria/nocturia with dilute urine. No glucose in the urine; BMP today for sugar, sodium and kidney function. Sickle cell is a known cause of a urine-concentrating problem; will have nephrology weigh in. Referral placed. Meanwhile spread fluids through the day rather than evening-heavy.

Addendum 4/17 15:50: BMP back. Glucose and sodium normal. Creatinine 1.21, a little up from his 1.0s. Included in referral.

conditions.label: Hyposthenuria secondary to sickle cell trait

documents.title: Nephrology Consultation
documents.author: nephrology
documents.body:
OUTSIDE NEPHROLOGY GROUP
New patient consultation, 08/27/2024
Referring: primary care physician

Reason: increased urination and nocturia.

Thank you for this referral. Mr. Mensah is a 26-year-old software developer with sickle cell, labelled trait since his newborn screen, and recurrent vaso-occlusive pain episodes since childhood. He describes roughly six months of higher urine volumes, waking at night to void, and a more recent general tiredness. He denies dysuria, fever and back pain. Your note mentions an earlier episode of fatigue in March 2023 that improved with consistent folate.

Medications: hydroxyurea 1000 mg daily; folic acid 1 mg daily.
Allergies: none known.
Family history: father carries sickle trait; maternal cousin with sickle cell disease; mother hypertensive.
Social: never smoker, no alcohol, software developer.

Examination: BP 130/80, pulse 78, temperature normal. Abdomen soft and non-tender. No costovertebral angle tenderness.

Data: sodium 140, potassium 4.2, creatinine 1.2 (eGFR mid 80s). Urine specific gravity 1.005. Your April values reviewed.

Impression:
1. Hyposthenuria related to sickle hemoglobin: a fixed inability to concentrate urine from medullary sickling, which explains his polyuria and nocturia.
2. Chronic kidney disease, stage 2.

Recommendations:
- Keep a steady fluid intake through the day; take most of it earlier and taper in the two hours before bed to cut down on night waking.
- He is prone to dehydration and cannot conserve water well: extra fluids in heat, exercise, or illness.
- Avoid NSAIDs.
- Creatinine and urine albumin/creatinine yearly through your office.
- No medication changes from our side. We are happy to see him again as needed.

Outside nephrology group

documents.title: Kidney doctor letter
documents.author: patient
documents.body: Did you get the letter from the kidney doctor? She said my kidneys can't concentrate urine because of the sickle cell and called it stage 2 kidney disease, which freaked me out a little. Is that something I need to worry about?

documents.title: RE: Kidney doctor letter
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: Got it, thanks for asking. Stage 2 means kidney function is mildly reduced but still good, and the main thing it changes is that we keep an eye on it once a year. The concentrating problem is what's causing the night trips. Biggest things on your end: steady fluids, more on hot days or when sick, and skip ibuprofen and naproxen. We'll add the urine protein test at your physical later this month.

documents.title: Annual Physical
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
Yearly exam. Nephrology letter reviewed with him. Shifting fluids earlier in the day has cut night voiding to about once. Energy fair. Flares unchanged in frequency.

Meds: hydroxyurea 1000 mg daily, folic acid 1 mg daily. NKDA. No NSAIDs.
Problems: sickle cell trait (per records) / sickle cell disease without crisis; recurrent vaso-occlusive pain crises; folate deficiency; hyposthenuria secondary to sickle cell trait; CKD stage 2.

Exam: Well. Pale conjunctivae, mild, anicteric. Heart RRR with flow murmur. Lungs clear. Abdomen soft, no CVA tenderness. Ext without edema or ulcers.

PHQ-2 1.

Plan: CBC/retic, CMP, urine albumin/creatinine. Flu and COVID vaccines today. Continue meds. Yearly kidney labs per nephrology.

documents.body: Unchanged from his usual. Continue.

documents.title: Preconception Counseling - Partner
documents.author: obstetrics
documents.body:
OUTSIDE OBSTETRICS & GYNECOLOGY PRACTICE
Preconception counseling, 03/09/2026. Copy to the partner's primary care physician.

Andre Mensah, 28, attended today with his wife, who is our patient, to plan for a pregnancy. Outside records from his primary care office reviewed: sickle cell trait per his records, history of vaso-occlusive pain episodes, hyposthenuria, folate deficiency, CKD stage 2. Medications: hydroxyurea 1000 mg daily, folic acid 1 mg daily. No known drug allergies. Family history: father with sickle trait, a maternal cousin with sickle cell disease, mother with hypertension. Never smoker, no alcohol; works as a software developer.

The couple's main question was whether a child of theirs could end up carrying the sickle gene without being ill from it, and how likely that is.

Counseling: we went over how the sickle hemoglobin change is passed on, one gene copy from each parent, and how the effect on a child depends on whether one or two altered copies are inherited. His wife's carrier status is the key unknown: her hemoglobin electrophoresis has not been done yet. We explained what each possible result would mean for their children in general terms and that we would go through the specific chances once her result is back. Genetic counseling referral offered for after her testing.

Plan: hemoglobin electrophoresis for his wife, ordered under her chart. Revisit as a couple when resulted. No changes to his care from our side.

Outside OB/GYN practice
